title: Access Control Administration
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 5: Identity and Access Management (IAM): Access Control Administration.

items: Service accounts — Used by applications; require strong passwords and monitoring
Shared accounts — Discouraged; undermine accountability
Privileged accounts — Administrator/root; require extra protection
Guest accounts — Limited access; disable when not needed
All accounts must have an identified owner responsible for access
Enforce least privilege — minimum access for job function
Watch for privilege creep — accumulation of unnecessary access over time
Privilege escalation — gaining higher privileges (horizontal or vertical)
Use role templates for consistent privilege assignment
Implement just-in-time (JIT) access for temporary elevated privileges

blocks.text: From Chapple: "Both excessive privileges and privilege creep violate the basic security principle of least privilege, and account reviews are effective at discovering these problems." Privilege Creep Prevention:

items: Regular access reviews/recertification
Role-based access control
Automated deprovisioning on role change
Manager approval for all access changes
Periodic reviews — Regular recertification of access rights (quarterly/annually)
User entitlement audits — Verify users have only needed access
Privileged account audits — More frequent than regular account reviews
Access logging — Record all access attempts (successful and failed)
Segregation of duties — Verify through access review

blocks.text: From Stewart: "Security personnel would perform user entitlement audits for privileged accounts much more often than user entitlement audits of regular user accounts." Access reviews should verify:

items: Users still need their current access
No orphaned accounts exist
Separation of duties is maintained
Privileged access is justified and monitored
Service accounts have current owners
PAM — Controls and monitors access for privileged accounts
Password vaulting — Stores privileged credentials in encrypted vault
Session recording — Records all privileged sessions for audit
Just-in-time access — Temporary elevation with automatic revocation
Privileged Access Workstations (PAW) — Dedicated, hardened systems for admin tasks

blocks.text: From Chapple: Third-party PAM services "integrate with Microsoft Active Directory. Once configured, users log onto the domain and access resources without logging on again." PAM reduces risk by:

items: Eliminating shared admin passwords
Providing audit trails for all privileged actions
Limiting the time window for privileged access
Detecting anomalous privileged behavior
